subject: Mid-contract capacity increase — flexible billing & pricing options for Helios Labs
messages:

Subject: Mid-contract capacity increase — quick question

Hi Grace,

We're projecting a higher Q3 usage curve for our GenAI search index and expect to need ~2.5x the committed tokens for July–September. Our renewals team asked if Redwood can offer a short mid-contract path (6 months) that keeps our current renewal date but gives temporary reserved capacity and a modest price incentive.

Key asks:
- Can we add a temporary committed uplift (6 months) that invoices pro-rata monthly?
- Is there a standard discounting approach for mid-contract top-ups?
- Can we co-term the uplift so everything still renews on 2029-01-01?

Attached: high-level forecast for Q3 (forecast_q3.xlsx).

We also have a procurement PO cadence (30-day net) — can you confirm billing lead times?

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-contract capacity increase — quick question

Hi Karen — thanks for the forecast and the clarity on timelines. Appreciate the attachment.

We can support the pattern you're describing. High-level options we typically propose for this use-case (short summary):

1) Temporary uplift (6 months) — reserved capacity added to your existing commit, invoiced monthly pro-rata. Pricing: list price for capacity + a volume uplift discount (example: 12% off incremental tokens for 6 months). No change to renewal date.

2) Accelerator voucher (prepaid credit) — Helios prepays an agreed voucher amount that covers burst usage; unused voucher balance rolls into the renewal pool. Offers better unit economics (example: ~18% effective discount vs pay-as-you-go) but requires prepaid invoice.

3) Partial annualization — move the uplift onto a committed, annualized tranche that is co-termed to 2029-01-01 with a graduated discount scale that favors longer locks. This is best if you want to lock price for the remainder of the year and simplify billing.

Immediate asks from our side to pick the right path:
- Ben (pricing) — could you confirm a proposed table for incremental token bands & discount tiers for a 6-month uplift?
- Marissa (legal) — any standard amendment template we should use to avoid full contract redline?
- Karen — do you have a procurement timeline for invoice/PO? 30 days workable?

If helpful, I can sketch a one-page amendment and a quick comparison table. I can also schedule a 30-minute cadence call tomorrow afternoon.

Best,
Grace
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Karen Liu <karen@helioslabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-contract capacity increase — quick question

Thanks, Grace. Karen — good visibility on the forecast. I ran a quick model and attached a pricing matrix with three practical offers (pricing_matrix_v3.csv). Summary: 

Offer A — Temporary uplift (6 months)- Incremental band: up to 2.5x current commit- Incremental discount: 12% off list on incremental tokens- Billing: monthly pro-rata on added commit- No change to renewal date

Offer B — Accelerator voucher (prepay)- Voucher size: equivalent to 6 months of expected incremental usage- Effective discount: 18% (prepay), unused credits roll into renewal bucket- Billing: one invoice, Net 30

Offer C — Partial annualize & co-term- Move 50% of uplift to co-termed annual tranche (ends 2029-01-01)- Discount: 15% on annualized portion, 10% on remaining 6-month tranche- Requires simple amendment (no major legal redlines expected)

Operational notes:
- We can support Net 30 PO for any of these; finance will require the PO before final invoice for voucher prepay.
- For co-terming we need a short amendment and a small billing note for mid-year proration.

Attachment: pricing_matrix_v3.csv (CSV, 14KB)

If you want, I can project monthly invoice examples for each option to make procurement sign-off easier.

Ben
Director, Renewals
ben_carter@redwoodinference.com

From: Karen Liu <karen@helioslabs.com>

Subject: Re: Mid-contract capacity increase — quick question

Grace / Ben — this is helpful. Procurement confirms Net 30 is fine. A couple of clarifying points before we commit:

1) Can the voucher option (Offer B) be structured so any unused credits during Q3 can be applied to usage through 2029-01-01? That helps our CFO justify the prepay.
2) For Offer C (partial annualize) — what happens if we materially cut usage after Q4? Any true-up or refund policy?
3) We will need SOC 2 in-scope confirmation and an updated Data Processing Addendum for the amendment. Can Marissa flag the minimal docs we need to attach to procurement?

Procurement has attached a short list of legal/compliance questions (procurement_questions.pdf). Happy to sign a short amendment via DocuSign once terms are agreed.

Thanks — we can sign off quickly if we get the voucher roll-forward confirmation plus the SOC 2 note.

Karen

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Mid-contract capacity increase — quick question

Karen — great, thanks for the clarifying questions. Short answers and next steps: 

1) Voucher roll-forward: yes — we can let unused voucher balance apply to usage through 2029-01-01. The voucher would then roll into the renewal bucket and count toward committed usage. We will show the mechanics in the amendment.

2) Partial annualize true-up: standard true-up policy applies — we annualize the committed portion; if actual usage is materially below the annualized commitment at renewal we do a usage reconciliation (no cash refunds, but credits can be applied or unused commitment carried as agreed). I asked Finance to outline thresholds for "material cut" (usually >40% below committed band).

3) SOC 2 & DPA: Marissa — can you confirm the checklist items procurement needs and attach SOC 2 attestation? Marissa: I've copied the procurement_questions.pdf to you.

Next steps:
- Ben: finalize the invoice examples for Offer B (voucher) and Offer C (partial annualize) and I'll circulate a one-page amendment draft.
- Marissa: confirm SOC2/DPA items and indicate whether the standard amendment template will suffice.
- Karen/procurement: if Net 30 PO process is aligned, I will send the DocuSign amendment and (if voucher chosen) a single prepaid invoice to process.

I'll attach a draft amendment stub to this thread for visibility: amendment_helios_v1.pdf (stub). HubSpot deal updated here: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/98341

Thanks all — I expect we can close this next week once procurement confirms voucher invoice timing.
